artist.mediums: Kerala mural painting (acrylic on canvas), watercolour, coloured pencil
artist.about:
Mahi (Maheshwaran) is a self-taught painter of Kerala murals, the temple-wall art of Kerala: gods and goddesses drawn in bold outline, filled with ochre, red, green and blue, and framed with rich ornament and lotus borders.

He began in Sydney in 2016 with a large Rasa Leela, Krishna dancing among the gopis, which travelled with him between Sydney and India for six years before he redrew and finished it in 2022. During the lockdown years he worked through a numbered series of paintings, learning the style's fine-line Rekhikam shading as he went, and decided to stay with traditional colours, traditional methods and free-hand drawing.

His work ranges from Krishna, Radha, Ganesha, Shiva and Shankaranarayana to Saraswati and Hanuman, mostly in acrylic on canvas, with some watercolour and coloured-pencil pieces.
artist.training: Self-taught; learnt the traditional techniques, such as Rekhikam fine-line shading, through practice and online lessons
artist.experience: Painting Kerala murals since 2016, in Sydney, India and California. Large works include the Rasa Leela (2016 to 2022) and The Butter Thieves.

works.title: Rasa Leela
works.description: Artist's note: every painting has its own destiny. I started this one in Sydney on 18 February 2016, and thought it was 80% done. It travelled with me to India and back, and waited at my parents' house for years. When I picked it up again I had grown as a painter, so I redrew the whole painting and finished it on 15 November 2022: born in Sydney, it finally reached its home.

works.medium: Kerala mural painting, acrylic on canvas
works.description: Artist's note: painting no. 4. With new-found confidence, it was time to go fully traditional. I added something of my own to the reference painting, some ornaments and the tree behind, and from here on decided to stick to traditional colours and methods, and only free-hand drawing.
